analysis: Batch contains only test changes. FlintAnswerStopTests.swift head lines 197-210 add maskCacheKeysFollowTheReturnedMasks: asserts FlintAnswerStopConstraint.allowsChainedDecode, maskCacheKey returns nil at remainingTokens 0, and keys map to identical allowed masks (matched state key -1 -> [0,1]). FlintNativeProtocolTests.swift patch hunks @@+209-227 and +267 add equivalent checks for FlintNativeProtocolConstraint across auto/none/required modes, nil key for out-of-range state and for exhausted state-cache. No production source is in this batch; the implied production behavior (mask caching keyed by constraint state, chained decode opt-in) lives in unsupplied ProviderCore constraint/CBv2 engine files. Security relevance: a mask-cache key collision between distinct masks could let a constrained decode emit tokens outside the Flint protocol (e.g., leak post-stop bytes or open tool frames), an output-integrity/availability concern under TB-007/T-007 rather than plaintext exposure; cache is per-constraint token masks, not the T-041 KV prefix cache, so no cross-tenant at-rest surface is evident. Tests check key->mask consistency only on sampled paths, not that keys are scoped per request/constraint instance; integration should verify in production source that maskCacheKey caches are not shared across requests with different tool schemas/stops (otherwise cross-request mask confusion), that nil keys disable caching, and that exhausted-state handling stays fail-closed. No regression identified from the supplied evidence.
